title: Design an Elevator System
reported: Design an elevator system: classes and responsibilities, elevator state, request handling, and the scheduling algorithm the controller uses to pick an elevator so customer wait time is minimised.

sources.passage:
If the next peak is higher, the positive height difference requires climbing-kit resources.
	• If the next peak is lower or equal, there is no climbing cost.
	• A helicopter can be used subject to a given limit and can cover an arbitrary height difference.
The objective was to determine the furthest peak reachable under the available resources.
This was an optimization/resource-allocation problem requiring identification of the appropriate algorithmic approach.

**Behavioral Questions**
Two behavioral questions were also asked during the DSA round.
One focused on:

Elevator System
Design an elevator system.

	• handling elevator requests

	• minimizing customer wait time

So the round was a combination of:
LLD + object modelling + scheduling/algorithmic reasoning.

Samsung R&D Research Noida conducted their Online Assessment in NIT PATNA on 15 September 2025.

Only CSE and ECE students whose cgpa more than 8.0 were allowed.

There were 3-4 people guarding the Examination and no mobile phones,smart watches,electronics things were allowed.

The Test was conducted on a Special software that was asked to download by the officials , That application will automatically detect any remote access or other external application for conducting valid examination

There was only a single question that has 50 test cases and we have to pass all the test cases. Time allotted was 3 hours.

Sprinklr | Product Engineering Intern | Gurugram | August 2023 [Offer]
I got an offer from Sprinklr on the first day of campus interviews. A little bit of background, I am a prefinal year student pursuing CSE in a tier-1 IIT. Here's a detailed walk-through of the entire interview process:

**Online Assessment (OA)**
Sprinklr shortlists candidates based on the performance in their OA. There were three questions, in which I was able to solve only the first two. For the third one (usually a very difficult question), all my peers submitted a brute-force solution which passed half of the test cases. Even though I wasn't able to submit the third question, I got shortlisted for the interview.

**Rounds**
There were 3 rounds, out of which the first 2 are technical, and finally a HR round.

**Round 1**
For the first 30 minutes of the interview, the interviewer emphasized on the projects I mentioned in my CV. I was particularly asked questions about a course project. I was asked to draw the entity-relationship diagram, entity and relation tables of the database that were used for the project.
Finally, a DSA question, which is of medium level. I figured out what data structure I would be needing, and I explained my solution approach on a shared IDE and implemented it at the end.

**Round 2**

This was the HR round. If you've made it till here you're almost in! The HR will first generally ask you about yourself, family hobbies etc. You can try to include stuff written in your CV for intro too. 
- After that they'll ask some behavourial questions like your experience working in teams, or what do your teammates think about you.
- How has been your college life, and why you want to pick SDE out of all other career options
- What do you think of the work-life balance, as in WFH vs Office, flexible hours or 9-5 etc. 
- Your dream company, apart from Sprinklr
- What do you think Sprinklr does? (I think the answer is supposed to be part of the PPT, otherwise do some research and tell what you find. Just make sure not to give a canned response)
- Which stack do you prefer, among
	- Backend (Java Spring with Mongo/Redis etc)
	- Frontend (JS/TS/React)
	- Mobile Dev (JS/React Native)
	- Machine Learning (Python)

There are supposed to be no wrong answers as such, so just be calm and just don't mess up
